correctness.rationale: The conditional two-new-voter gain–loss coupling gives the exact binomial factor times signed powers of p(1−p); combining equal p(1−p) values is explicit. The exponential-polynomial real-zero bound follows inductively from Rolle’s theorem with distinct nonzero rates. Each integer-sign reversal forces a separate continuous root. The polynomial Q_d construction interlaces exactly d−1 roots with d successive sampling arguments, and its signed coefficients are represented by legal strictly positive mixing weights with conditional competences in (0,1). As t tends to zero, the dominant favorable state has mass and competence tending to one, while covariance is Var(P)>0. The packaged exact finite checker is supporting rather than infinite proof.

value.rationale: Correlated information invalidates simplistic Condorcet jury-size monotonicity even with high average juror accuracy. This theorem gives a sharp structural complexity law: each effective latent reliability scale permits at most one extra beneficial/harmful jury-enlargement reversal; an explicit valid voting distribution attains every possible complexity. The result is not a routine numeric perturbation and distinguishes reliability heterogeneity from mere correlation or mean competence. Limits: binary truthful exchangeable votes, finite support and odd majorities only.
